business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Document Automation and E-Signature Authentication

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (US-derived) with Marshallese customary law elements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (Title 53, Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act 2018; Financial Intelligence Unit (Beneficial Ownership and Control) Regulations 2018, as administered by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit and the Office of the Registrar of Corporations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authenticated copy of beneficial owner's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the beneficial owner's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified recent proof of residential address of beneficial owner (utility or government-issued record)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or government agency in beneficial owner's domicile

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate registry extract and certificate of good standing for any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry of the UBO entity's incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming provenance of funds for initial capitalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship banking institution of the beneficial owner

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories and ultimate controlling persons must be screened against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and RMI FIU domestic watchlist before incorporation. Positive PEP or sanctions matches require enhanced due diligence and senior compliance approval; adverse matches result in refusal of the engagement. Screening must be refreshed within 30 days before the name clearance filing and re-run upon any change in UBO, in accordance with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry (Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro) – agent-administered electronic filing portal; no direct public incorporation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official languages are Marshallese and English. The registry only processes company names in English or Latin-script transliteration. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated and the transliteration certified by the registered agent; corporate suffixes must be in English.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On name rejection, the applicant receives written reasons from the Registrar. An administrative extension of a reserved name may be obtained for a further 30 days by filing a renewal application before the original reservation expires. A rejection appeal is made by filing a Request for Administrative Reconsideration within 14 calendar days of rejection, together with the applicable fee and written submissions; the Registrar must issue a decision within 10 business days. A further appeal lies to the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 30 days of the reconsideration denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A separate virtual office is permitted for correspondence only, and may not substitute for the statutory registered office, which must be the physical address of the licensed RMI registered agent in Majuro. Non-resident LegalTech SaaS operations with no in-country employees are permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk non-resident LegalTech BC with no RMI-source income, assessed annual probability is below 5%; it rises above 25% upon suspicious transaction reports, FIU outreach, or failure to maintain current UBO records at the registered agent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing and certificate of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee for a non-resident Business Corporation
Statutory annual franchise tax based on authorized share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered office and registered agent services (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial agent fee; prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register, PEP/sanctions screening, and AML/CFT compliance setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille/consular legalization, and international courier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, competent apostille authority, and courier provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial and apostille tariff plus international courier charge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990, Title 27 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC), incorporating provisions on corporate formation, registered office and agent, share capital, directors and officers; Business License Act 1990 (Title 60 MIRC); Income Tax Act (Title 44 MIRC); Electronic Transactions Act 2005.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (MARIS electronic registry portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (statutory articles form prescribed under the Business Corporations Act; filed via the MARIS portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital, no minimum authorized capital, and no escrow account requirement. Shares may be issued with par or no-par value; consideration may be money, services, or property as valued by the board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Certificate of Incorporation filed with the Registrar of Corporations is hereby ratified and approved. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be the business address of the licensed registered agent recorded in the Mandatory Directory, and said agent is appointed for the ensuing year. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the issuance of 100 shares of no-par Common Stock to the initial subscriber at the stated consideration is ratified, and the Secretary shall record the same in the share register. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each empowered to open bank accounts, execute payment processor agreements, file statutory returns, and attest corporate instruments under the corporate seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations - MARIS online name search and reservation window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the MARIS registry to confirm the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing entities. Submit a name reservation request in English; the Registrar will reserve an acceptable name for 90 days pending filing of the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, resubmit using two pre-cleared alternative names from the search results; reinstatement of the application carries no additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Licensed Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed corporate service providers approved by the Registrar of Corporations (private agent market)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered agent acceptance letter and Mandatory Directory engagement with a Marshall Islands-licensed agent. The agent must maintain a physical street address in the Republic and accept service of process on behalf of the corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the designated agent declines, execute a replacement engagement with another licensed agent and file the notice of change of registered agent with the Registrar before the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the execution jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator completes the statutory Certificate of Incorporation setting out the corporate name, registered office and agent, authorized share structure, and purposes. The certificate is signed and dated by the incorporator before a notary; the notarial attestation must accompany the filing where execution occurs outside the Republic.
required_dossiers: Notarial attestation (or apostille) of incorporator signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Registrar identifies a defect, execute a corrected certificate in the same statutory form and re-submit; corrections requested by the Registrar are processed without re-payment of the government filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations - MARIS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Certificate of Incorporation together with the registered agent acceptance and the USD 250 government filing fee. Upon payment clearance and compliance review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and opens the public corporate record.
required_dossiers: First page of the Mandatory Directory (registered office and agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, amend the certificate in accordance with the Registrar's written observations and re-file; the Registrar will issue the certificate within three business days of the corrected submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting and Pro-Forma Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the corporation (internal governance; no regulatory counters involved)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator convenes the organizational meeting. The board adopts the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, ratifies the incorporation filing, adopts the registered office, approves the share subscription, and appoints officers. Resolutions must be recorded in minutes or by unanimous written consent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director cannot attend, the action is valid as unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting, which is expressly permitted under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Directory and Officer Particulars Lodgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations - Mandatory Directory records through the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Mandatory Directory listing the registered office, registered agent, directors, and officers within the statutory period. The directory is part of the public record and must be updated within 21 days of any change in officers, registered office, or agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the directory is returned for incomplete officer details, file a corrected directory page within five business days; clerical corrections carry no penalty when submitted before the due date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Annual Compliance and Non-Resident Tax-Exempt Status Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (annual registration) and Ministry of Finance (tax status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the annual compliance cycle commencing on the anniversary of incorporation, including the annual registration fee and the mandatory update of the Mandatory Directory. File a non-resident domestic corporation declaration confirming that no business is conducted in the Marshall Islands, which supports exemption from the Business License Act and from income tax on foreign-source revenue.
required_dossiers: Corporate resolutions for bank account and Stripe/credit-card payment processor onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual registration falls due during formation, pay the fee plus statutory late penalty within the grace period to keep the corporate record in good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Investment and Trade - Business Licensing Division (exemption applies to non-resident domestic corporations)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - Non-Resident Domestic Corporation exemption under the Business License Act 1990; cloud document automation and e-signature authentication services are lawful without a sectoral license under the Electronic Transactions Act 2005.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Republic of the Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI-EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Low-Impact Digital Service Activity under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 2001, Regulation 5(1)(a); no physical works, land use, or construction in the Marshall Islands, therefore no EIA Registration or Full EIA Report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the enterprise generates no point-source wastewater or VOC emissions in-country. Any end-of-life IT equipment or e-waste arising from remote operations must be handled through approved recyclers consistent with RMI-EPA solid waste management standards; no discharge permits are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not triggered - the corporation maintains no physical premises in the Marshall Islands beyond the registered agent's licensed office, which holds its own fire safety and structural clearances. No employees are physically stationed in-country; therefore no fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or workplace clearance is required from the Majuro Fire Brigade or the Occupational Health and Safety administration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Revenue and Taxation Division, Majuro; corporate registration and good-standing certification are administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations under the Ministry of Finance. Filings are effected exclusively through licensed RMI registered agents; no direct public tax e-filing portal exists for non-resident entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP for a foreign-owned non-resident Business Corporation (BC): (1) appoint a licensed RMI registered agent; (2) file Articles of Incorporation with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations via the agent; (3) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, which evidences valid corporate existence, registered office, and registered agent; (4) obtain an annual Certificate of Good Standing for bank onboarding and cross-border contracting; (5) no TIN is procured at incorporation because a non-resident BC earning no RMI-source income is statutorily outside the income tax and Gross Revenue Tax net; (6) if local RMI activity is commenced, file the GRT registration with the Revenue and Taxation Division, obtain a TIN, and register with the RMI Social Security Administration for any RMI-resident employees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — A non-resident Business Corporation is treated as a tax-exempt offshore entity: income tax applies only on a territorial basis to RMI-source income, the entity is outside the scope of the Gross Revenue Tax, and no VAT/GST exists. The exemption remains conditional on carrying on no business in the RMI and deriving no income from RMI sources.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI law does not adopt US-style check-the-box entity classification or OECD hybrid-mismatch elections. Available statutory mechanisms: (1) designation as a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) under the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Act, which expressly confers exemption from Gross Revenue Tax and local income tax; (2) continuation or re-domestication of a foreign corporation into the RMI under the Business Corporations Act; (3) registration as a Foreign Maritime Entity (FME) for shipping activities; (4) selection of corporate governance and registered-agent arrangements under the Business Corporations Act. No hybrid-mismatch elective regime is legislated.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST is legislated in the RMI. The only turnover-based indirect levy is the 3% Gross Revenue Tax (GRT), chargeable on gross revenue derived from business activity conducted within the Marshall Islands; customs import duty is levied separately under the Customs Tariff Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST as no such tax exists. GRT registration is required only for businesses conducting activity within the RMI whose annual gross revenue exceeds USD 50,000; a non-resident LegalTech SaaS provider with no RMI nexus has no registration threshold to satisfy.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API reporting mandate exists in the RMI. Indirect tax and customs compliance remains document-based: commercial invoice, packing list, cargo manifest, and bill of lading/air waybill. The RMI Customs Service has not deployed mandatory continuous transaction controls or SAF-T style reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. The RMI does not operate a VAT/GST export zero-rating or refund mechanism. Exports of physical goods from the RMI are not subject to export duty, and cross-border digital services supplied by a non-resident BC (e.g., cloud document automation, e-signature authentication, LegalTech SaaS) are wholly outside the RMI territorial tax net; no indirect tax is chargeable on such services and no refund substantiation is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Outward Cargo Manifest / Customs Export Declaration (required only for physical exports; digital SaaS services require no customs filing)
Commercial Invoice stating exporter, consignee, export commodity code, and transaction value
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing international transport
Inward Remittance Certificate (not required — the RMI imposes no foreign-exchange control or FX repatriation regime)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT refund or export zero-rating regime exists, so there is no export-refund clawback exposure. General enforcement rules: (1) under the Gross Revenue Tax Act, late filing, underpayment, or fraudulent returns attract statutory penalty plus interest and possible criminal fines for active local businesses; (2) under the Income Tax Act, tax evasion is subject to criminal fines and imprisonment; (3) under the Customs Act, false export declarations may trigger seizure, forfeiture, and administrative penalties; (4) under the Business Corporations Act, failure to maintain a registered agent and pay annual renewal fees results in administrative dissolution and loss of limited liability. All such exposure is moot for a non-resident BC deriving no RMI-source income, whose only ongoing compliance obligation is annual corporate renewal and good-standing certification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands does not maintain a domestic central bank or separate foreign-exchange administration. Banking supervision, licensing, and AML/CFT oversight are administered by the Marshall Islands Banking Commission (MIBC), a statutory body operating under the Ministry of Finance, pursuant to the Banking Act 1970 (as amended) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2020. The U.S. Federal Reserve System functions as the de facto monetary authority because the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender under the Compact of Free Association; all USD clearing ultimately settles through the Federal Reserve.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands operates a fully dollarized economy with no exchange-control statute. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible; the repatriation of capital, remittance of dividends, management fees, and liquidation proceeds by non-resident Business Corporations requires no MIBC approval, no exchange-licence, and no prior authorisation certificate. The binding operational constraint is not legal convertibility but correspondent-bank due diligence, because every USD wire transfer is cleared through one or more U.S. intermediary banks that independently apply OFAC sanctions screening and enhanced KYC thresholds to Marshall Islands entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation exists in the Marshall Islands. Export receipts, SaaS subscription revenue, software licensing fees, and royalties from the cloud document automation business are not subject to mandatory conversion ratios, repatriation timelines, or holding-period requirements. Foreign-currency receipts may be freely retained in multi-currency accounts, swapped, or converted to USD at the entity's discretion through any licensed commercial bank, and there is no requirement to route proceeds through the domestic banking system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of the Federated States of Micronesia – Majuro Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-rated feasibility with strict legal constraints. Non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporations may open USD-denominated accounts with qualifying foreign Electronic Money Institutions and digital-banking platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer Business) where those platforms accept the RMI corporate form; however, no Marshall Islands fintech charter or domestic EMI licensing exists, and the Marshall Islands Banking Act 1970 prohibits any unlicensed deposit-taking business within Marshall Islands territory. Accordingly, onboarding to a foreign EMI is legally permissible only if the EMI does not solicit deposits inside the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the EMI holds a valid license in its home jurisdiction, and the MHC entity executes the EMI's client agreement as a non-resident remote customer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI corporate law does not mandate a face-to-face director interview for domestic account opening, but in practice tier-1 local banks require either at least one director's physical appearance at the Majuro or Ebeye branch, or the submission of a notarised signature card, Certified Certificate of Good Standing, Certificate of Incumbency, and certified passport copies channelled through the Registered Agent. Remote onboarding is accepted for pure equity-funding accounts provided the RMI Registered Agent holds an original power-of-attorney and the beneficial-owner identities are disclosed to the MIBC-regulated bank. International banks in Singapore, Hong Kong, the United States, or the UAE generally impose an in-person director interview or a high-grade video-identity verification with a compliance officer, and a director will typically need to travel to the account-opening jurisdiction or attend a foreign bank's representative office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt non-resident corporation presumption of shell activity / absence of economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Business Law Registry; active-status extract; Registered Agent confirmation; IRS Form W-8BEN-E; audited or management-verified financial statements; an economic-substance memorandum describing the cloud document automation and e-signature authentication business; commercial SaaS contracts; subscriber-count dashboard; SOC 2 Type II report; and a board resolution designating the account purpose and settlement flows.

Direct and indirect ownership-chain diagram; shareholder ledger; corporate register extracts; certified passport copies of every ultimate beneficial owner; any trust deed or holding-company constitutional documents; source-of-wealth narrative and supporting bank reference letter from the parent company's bank; plus a search confirmation against the RMI/POA and international sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated country-risk and sanctions reputational concern associated with a shipping-favoured flag-state jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-news and sanctions-screening reports demonstrating no adverse hits; payment-traffic evidence generated by the Stripe and credit-card acquiring platform showing genuine SaaS revenue; ISIC 6201 and NAICS 541199 industry classification certificate; utility or web-infrastructure invoices confirming cloud architecture; explanation of the office or virtual-address presence; and, if applicable, a Singapore or UAE operational-nexus narrative with employment or contractor records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from shareholders shall be remitted as SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers (or Fedwire for domestic U.S. remitters) with the purpose-of-payment code reflecting equity contribution — generally '610' under U.S. correspondent-bank enhanced mapping, or 'LOAN'/'EQTI' as accepted by the receiving bank. The wire narrative must state: 'Contribution to Paid-In Capital — Non-Resident Business Corporation, ISIC 6201.' The receiving bank's KYC file must be pre-loaded with the board resolution authorising share issuance, an updated share-register extract, the RMI Registered Agent certificate, and a source-of-funds declaration. For any USD transfer that triggers a U.S. intermediary-bank compliance review, the treasury team shall supply the parent-company audited balance sheet and the executed subscription agreement within 24 hours of the funds hold notice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for LegalTech SaaS operations shall use the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for international vendor licensing fees, external legal counsel, Registered Agent fees, shareholder distributions, and non-US contractor payments; (ii) Fedwire and ACH for all U.S.-domiciled payments, including AWS cloud hosting, marketing platforms, and U.S. professional-service providers; (iii) Visa and Mastercard card-rail settlement through the Stripe acquiring corridor for both inbound customer collections and outbound recurring software subscriptions or ad-hoc procurement; and (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit only for physical hardware procurement or enterprise infrastructure supply contracts, since SaaS licensing itself does not involve title documents. Every outbound MT103 must pass a dual-authorisation treasury control, an OFAC/consolidated sanctions-list negative screen of the beneficiary, and an FX-rate or fee reasonableness check before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward Contracts (USD against EUR, GBP, AUD, JPY, and CAD) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or an FX master agreement with a licensed international bank counterparty
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies lacking onshore forward markets or where local exchange-control regulations prohibit deliverable hedging without a domestic banking licence
Cross-Currency Swaps (FX Swaps / CCS) to mitigate the liquidity mismatch between USD subscription inflows and EUR/GBP/AUD-denominated operating costs
Vanilla FX Options (Puts and Calls) permitted under the treasury risk policy and executed only with a bank rated investment-grade or above

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Renewal Report and Franchise Tax Return (BCA Section 91 Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (Office of Financial and Commercial Regulation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the month of the incorporation anniversary each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the annual fee per commenced month of delay; persistent non-filing beyond 90 days from the due date triggers administrative strike-off and loss of legal capacity; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Continuation Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agent (continuity record filed with the Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual report deadline (anniversary month); immediate notification to the Registrar upon agent resignation or office relocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent and a registered office in the Marshall Islands constitutes grounds for involuntary dissolution; the Registrar may declare the corporation in default and strike it off without further notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) and Shareholding Re-Confirmation (AML/CFT KYC Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent acting as AML/CFT compliance gatekeeper under the Registered Agents Licensing Act 2014
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the anniversary date of incorporation; within 30 days following any share transfer that changes a 25% or greater beneficial ownership position
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Stale or inaccurate UBO records constitute a regulatory compliance breach; the registered agent must cease acting or report the deficiency, and the corporation may be deregistered; fines of up to US$20,000 apply for failure to respond to lawful information requests.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit applies to a non-resident Business Corporation under the BCA. An audit becomes compulsory only if required by the articles or bylaws, by a special shareholder resolution, by a lender or investor covenant, or where the corporation holds a separate regulated activity license such as banking, insurance, or trust business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting framework for statutory or tax filings; voluntary financial statements may be prepared under IFRS or US GAAP; books and records must accurately reflect the financial position and material transactions, with no public filing of accounts required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent conducts an annual KYC cycle confirming the identity of every natural person holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the issued share capital or exercising ultimate effective control; any share transfer requires an immediate instrument of transfer and a beneficial ownership update within 30 days; consolidated UBO records are retained by the agent and disclosed to the Financial Intelligence Unit or Registrar only upon lawful statutory request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Mortgages and Charges (if any created)
Minute Book of Shareholder and Board Meetings
Registered Agent's Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Non-resident Business Corporation: 40% of gross income derived from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Income Tax Act 1989, s.141). Resident/domestic corporation: 11% of net RMI-source income (s.142). The subject entity, a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) earning exclusively foreign-source SaaS and e-signature revenue, bears an effective RMI income tax rate of 0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exclusion of non-RMI-source income for NRDCs under the Business Corporations Act; no capital gains tax; no wealth or net worth tax; no estate/inheritance tax; no RMI gross receipts or branch profits tax on foreign receipts; legacy International Business Company Act 20-year written tax-holiday exemptions where still in force. The LegalTech SaaS subscription model (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541199) qualifies for the 0% effective rate only if no customer, employee, server, or management activity is physically located in the Marshall Islands.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CIT-MH-1) filed through the RMI Revenue and Taxation Division electronic filing system (eTax/RMI). A nil declaration is permitted where no RMI-source income arises. For an NRDC with purely foreign-source income, Form CIT-MH-1 is not compulsory; the mandatory annual compliance filing is the Business Corporations Act Annual Report filed with the RMI Registrar of Corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Filings are due once per fiscal year; no quarterly installments are imposed on tax-exempt NRDC income. The BCA Annual Report is also an annual requirement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form CIT-MH-1: on or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; an extension of up to three additional months is available upon written application before the original due date. BCA Annual Report: on or before 31 March each year in respect of the preceding calendar year, with a late penalty of US$50 per month (maximum US$250) and risk of administrative strike-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero where all revenue arises from cloud document automation and e-signature authentication contracts performed outside the RMI. Any RMI-based customer, RMI resident partner, or RMI-issued invoice converts receipts to RMI-source income and destroys the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross income excluded from the RMI tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a global revenue schedule and a statement that NRDC status under the Business Corporations Act is in force. For a foreign-owned BC conducting no business in the RMI, 100% of SaaS subscription fees and e-signature transaction fees fall in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and expenses allocable to RMI-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where Box 1a is zero, enter zero. If RMI-source income is present, allocate direct costs on a pro-rata revenue basis; overhead, hosting, and developer salaries must be supported by contemporaneous records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net RMI-source taxable income (Box 1a minus Box 2).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to a qualifying NRDC; annotate 'N/A - NRDC foreign-source only' and attach the BCA exemption certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate election: 11% resident / 40% non-resident gross.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an NRDC, do not elect either rate; instead, write 'NRDC - 0% effective RMI tax' and cite Income Tax Act s.141(e) exclusion and BCA non-resident election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax due, credits, and declaration of nil liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File a signed declaration under penalty of perjury confirming the absence of RMI-source income; retain the executed copy for at least six years for the Registered Agent and FSC audit files.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid RMI tax per month or fraction thereof, capped at 25%; additional daily surcharge of US$25 per day of default (maximum US$1,000). Late payment interest: 1% per month. Deliberate non-filing: civil penalty equal to 50% of the tax due; criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act ss.201-204 exposes the entity to fines up to US$10,000 and responsible officers to imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory final withholding tax of 10% on dividends paid out of RMI-source profits to non-resident shareholders. Effective rate for the subject NRDC: 0%, because distributions are made exclusively from foreign-source accumulated profits and the RMI imposes no withholding on such non-RMI-source dividends. The paying corporation has no statutory duty to withhold absent RMI-source earnings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no general comprehensive double tax agreement network; the operative instrument is the Agreement with the United States implementing Article IX of the Compact of Free Association, which may eliminate double taxation on US-RMI income flows. Administrative protocol: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and NRDC status certificate from the Revenue and Taxation Division and the Registrar of Corporations; (ii) complete the relevant IRS Form W-8BEN-E or RMI Schedule WHT-R claim; (iii) deliver the treaty relief claim to the paying agent no fewer than 15 calendar days before the distribution; (iv) maintain beneficial-ownership declarations, board minutes, and economic substance records for all treaty benefit claims; and (v) renew the TRC annually before the RMI fiscal year-end.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI-source rate: 10% final withholding on royalties for the use of intellectual property and on interest paid to non-residents. The US Compact arrangement can reduce US-source, but not RMI-source, taxation to 0% in qualifying cases. The subject SaaS entity should ensure that trademark, software, and e-signature technology royalties are received from foreign licensees only; inbound licensing agreements must be priced at arm's length and the aggregate debt-to-equity ratio maintained at or below 3:1 to avoid thin-capitalization re-characterization of interest into dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The RMI has not enacted express Local File / Master File monetary thresholds; the Revenue and Taxation Division applies OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines by interpretive analogy. Prudent compliance benchmark: prepare and retain a Local File where aggregate related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 per fiscal year, and a Master File / Country-by-Country-reportable group file where consolidated group revenue exceeds USD 50,000,000, consistent with BEPS Action 13 expectations for a low-risk LegalTech SaaS group.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. The Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations (ESR 2019) and RMI Financial Services Commission guidance require every RMI business corporation carrying on a relevant activity to satisfy: (a) direction and management in the RMI, evidenced by quorum board meetings and minutes maintained in the RMI; (b) core income-generating activities (CIGA) performed in the RMI; and (c) adequate employees, physical premises, and operating expenditure proportionate to the income generated. A legal contract automation and e-signature SaaS entity with no RMI staff is at high risk of reclassification as an IP-holding or pure equity vehicle, which mandates strict CIGA performance in the RMI; annual ESR notification and, where applicable, substance reporting are mandatory for all RMI business corporations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating RMI-source turnover, falsely claiming NRDC status while deriving income from RMI customers, backdating board minutes and licensing contracts to manufacture foreign-source characterization, or destroying revenue records to misallocate SaaS fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Felony conviction: fine up to US$10,000 per count and/or imprisonment up to five years; civil penalty equal to 50% of the understated tax plus monthly interest at 1%; forfeiture of the exemption and recomputation of tax at 40% of gross RMI-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or approve fictitious foreign-source schemes are personally liable under the Business Corporations Act fraud exception to limited liability, jointly and severally for restitution, and subject to RMI travel bans, asset seizures, and disqualification orders barring future directorships for up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / ESR Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a nominal NRDC with zero RMI presence while deriving revenue from a relevant activity; failing to file the annual ESR notification; submitting boilerplate CIGA schedules that misclassify automated cloud contract generation as purely administrative non-core work.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR penalty up to US$10,000 per failure and US$100,000 for recurring or deliberate non-compliance; administrative strike-off by the Registrar; referral to the EU Code of Conduct Group and OECD Forum for Harmful Tax Practices, triggering listing as a non-cooperative jurisdiction and consequential 15% penalty or complete loss of the tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the RMI registered agent face liability for knowing participation in a sham: mandatory compensatory payments, five-year director bans, license revocation for the registered agent, and potential criminal prosecution for false declarations made to the RMI Financial Services Commission.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Stripe and credit card settlements without customer due diligence, enabling anonymous API misuse, onboarding sanctioned counterparties through the e-signature platform, failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register, or neglecting suspicious transaction reports for unusual SaaS payment patterns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2005 (as amended): criminal fine up to US$50,000 on individual officers and US$200,000 on the corporate entity; imprisonment up to ten years for willful money laundering; suspension or revocation of the FSC operating license; inclusion of the entity in national AML risk advisories.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal pecuniary penalties, freezing of personal bank accounts in support of confiscation proceedings, extradition exposure through US-RMI Mutual Legal Assistance channels, and automatic failure of the FSC 'Fit and Proper' test, permanently disqualifying the director from any licensed financial activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Social Security Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying RMI-resident software developers as foreign independent contractors to avoid RMI Social Security and Medicare withholding; failing to withhold the 10% statutory tax on RMI-source dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents; failing to register as a withholding employer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid withholding tax is a first-priority trust-fund claim; failure to deduct and remit triggers a 100% penalty on the unwithheld tax plus interest at 1% per month; social security delinquency incurs surcharges up to 50% of unpaid contributions and criminal prosecution of the responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person doctrine applies to directors and the statutory controller: joint and several personal liability for withheld but unremitted taxes, enforced by asset seizure, exit-permit/departure objections preventing travel from the RMI, and a ten-year bar on appointment to any RMI corporate or financial entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Conveyance / Veil Piercing in Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends or upstreaming shareholder loans while the NRDC is insolvent, routing distributions through nominee shell accounts to obscure ultimate beneficial ownership, or breaching RMI banking disclosure covenants by commingling personal and corporate card proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the BCA dividend restrictions, an unlawful or insolvent distribution is void; directors are personally liable to restore the full distribution amount plus interest; courts may award punitive damages up to treble the fraudulent transfer for bad-faith conveyances to shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Liability is joint and several with no contribution among conspiring directors; ex parte asset-preservation orders and travel restrictions are routinely granted; nominee directors who sign false ownership declarations face up to seven years' imprisonment for perjury before RMI judicial authorities.
